cards.name: White Magical Hat
cards.effect: When this card inflicts Battle Damage to your opponent's Life Points, your opponent discards 1 card randomly from his/her hand.

cards.name: Robbin' Goblin
cards.effect: Each time a monster you control inflicts Battle Damage to your opponent, your opponent discards 1 random card.

behavior: White Magical Hat only plans after positive battle damage from that face-up monster; it may resolve after the source reaches its physical owner's Graveyard.
Robbin' Goblin reacts to each positive battle-damage event from a monster controlled by its team; every face-up copy receives a distinct activation receipt.
Both effects discard one random card from the active physical opponent seat's private hand, not the inactive partner's reserve hand.
The host injects the random-index function; the adapter does not select a target and never substitutes another card.
Robbin' Goblin must remain face-up in its controller team's backrow at resolution; negation, empty hand, stale events and duplicate receipts are handled explicitly.
The physical UID owner is preserved when a stolen attacker is destroyed; discarded card moves to the shared team Graveyard without creating or granting inventory.
A hand above six is not normalized here; the ordinary End Phase owns the hand-limit discard.
implementation.integrationBoundary: Isolated TagDuel adapter only. No catalog registration, card certification, central resolver, Discord command, persistent player data or deployment changes.

focusedScenarios: White Magical Hat random discard from active opponent seat
source leaves field after damage and physical-owner Graveyard routing
source already in owner's Graveyard when event is delivered
effect damage/zero damage/incomplete Damage Step/turn/team rejection
Robbin' Goblin triggers for any team-controlled attacker
negation, empty hand, duplicate receipt and invalid RNG
hand above six remains for End Phase
3+3 zones, Main Deck 20 and 30, Extra Deck 5 and overflow

limitations: Cards are not registered in engine-v9 on the shared branch; the production adapter remains pinned to official passcodes and tests use admitted fixture IDs.
The host must emit a genuine post-Damage-Step battle-damage event, supply the active opponent seat through current TagDuel rotation, and inject the duel RNG.
Central trigger wiring, catalog admission, certification and Discord command integration remain separate work and require the M61 resolver handoff.
